lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Guided practice B: simulation and model limitations

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Read once, then cover the example and try the guided set from memory.

items.prompt: A meal has 3 main dish options and 2 side options. How many different meals are possible?

steps: Identify the favorable outcomes and the total possible outcomes.
Write the probability as a reduced fraction, or use it to predict or evaluate a count.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A probability model predicts a fair 5-section spinner lands on a chosen section about 18 times in 90 spins. A simulation of 90 spins landed on that section 17 times. How does the simulated count compare to the model's prediction?
An event has a probability of 1/2. How would you describe how likely the event is to happen?
choices: equally likely to happen or not happen

items.prompt: A spinner was spun 60 times and landed on blue 17 times. Based on this experiment, what is the experimental probability of landing on blue?
A bag has 2 red, 4 blue, and 7 green marbles. If one marble is drawn at random, what is the theoretical probability of drawing red, P(red)?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A fair coin is flipped and a spinner with 5 equal sections numbered 1 to 5 is spun. What is the probability of getting tails on the coin and landing on 1 on the spinner?
A meal is made by choosing one main dish from 2 options and one side dish from 5 options. How many different meals are possible?

A probability model predicts a fair 5-section spinner lands on a chosen section about 43 times in 215 spins. A simulation of 215 spins landed on that section 35 times. How does the simulated count compare to the model's prediction?
An event has a probability of 1. How would you describe how likely the event is to happen?
choices: equally likely to happen or not happen

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: A spinner was spun 40 times and landed on blue 3 times. Based on this experiment, what is the experimental probability of landing on blue?
A bag has 4 red, 7 blue, and 8 green marbles. If one marble is drawn at random, what is the theoretical probability of drawing red, P(red)?
